title: Reverse a String Without Library Calls
statement:
Given a string `s`, print the string with its characters in reverse order.

You must produce the reversal yourself: do **not** use any built-in reverse function (such as `reverse`, `reversed`, `[::-1]`, `StringBuilder.reverse`, or `std::reverse`). Swapping characters with two pointers or walking the string from the back are both acceptable.

The string contains no whitespace, so it is read as a single token.

**Follow-up:** Do the reversal in place, using O(1) extra memory beyond the character array itself.
inputFormat: A single line containing the string `s` (no whitespace).
outputFormat: Print the reversed string on one line.
constraints: s consists of printable ASCII characters other than whitespace

examples.explanation: Reading the letters from the last to the first gives e, g, r, o, f.
Digits and punctuation are treated like any other character and simply move to the mirrored position.
A single character is its own reversal.

hints: Which character ends up at position 0 of the answer? And at position 1?
Put one pointer at the start and one at the end, swap the characters they point to, and move them toward each other until they meet.
Building the answer by repeatedly adding a character to the front of a string can take O(n^2) time because each addition copies the string. Prefer a character array or a list.
